blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: linked list — A structure where each item contains data and a link to another item.
pointer — A value identifying the location of another item.
start pointer — The index of the first item in the list.
next pointer — The index of the next item.
null — A marker meaning no next item.
traverse — Visit each item by following links.

blocks.title: Start pointer
blocks.text: The first logical item is stored at index 2, not necessarily index 0.

blocks.title: Follow next pointers
blocks.text: Use -1 as null in code. Each pointer decides the next index.

blocks.title: Insert at the front
blocks.text: The new item points to the old first item, then start changes.

blocks.title: Remove after current
blocks.text: The pointer bypasses one node. The array data itself does not need to shift.

blocks.title: Worked example · Traverse Alex → Ben → Cara → Daisy
blocks.text: using System; public class Program { public static void Main() { string[] data = {"Ben", "Daisy", "Alex", "Cara"}; int[] next = {3, -1, 0, 1}; int start = 2; int current = start; while (current != -1) { Console.WriteLine(data[current]); current = next[current]; } } }
